articles.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. Paired targeted interventions show that false-drop causes significantly greater degradation than false-keep, while a non-deleting baseline can still fail when incorrect labels steer

articles.title: LoRAWeaver: Directional Adapter Routing in LoRA Representation Space
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are expensive to update through full retraining. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning reduces the cost of adaptation, but repeated adaptation creates a growing pool of task-specific LoRA adapters. This pool complicates adapter selection during inference. Existing routing and encoder-based methods often require retraining when new adapters are added, which limits their use in dynamic settings. articles.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medication prediction from electronic health records is a fixed vocabulary structured prediction problem, yet recent clinical RAG systems often treat it like open ended case based reasoning: retrieve similar patient admissions and ask an LLM to infer a medication set. This retrieval object is indirect the model receives retrieved patient records while the target is a discrete set of medication class labels. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.17398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The appropriate governing norms and principles for the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) often depend on cultural context and deployment application. articles.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
articles.summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia. Keeping regular times for sleeping, eating, and other activities may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood, sleep, and overall health.

articles.title: Republicans experience worse mental health in Democratic neighborhoods, study finds
articles.summary: A large national study finds that Republicans living in heavily Democratic neighborhoods report higher rates of anxiety, depression, and loneliness. Democrats, however, show similar mental health regardless of their neighborhood's political makeup.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
articles.summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect memory.

articles.title: Family ties emerge as a key link between poverty and teen well-being in Taiwanese study
articles.summary: Among more than 1,300 Taiwanese adolescents living in poverty, those facing more material hardship reported poorer family relationships and more psychological distress. Family ties appeared to be the most consistent link between deprivation and adolescents’ well-being.

articles.title: Psychologists map the connection between dark personality traits and romantic jealousy
articles.summary: New psychological research reveals how aggressive personality traits are channeled into romantic jealousy. The findings suggest that hostility often expresses itself through an obsessive, possessive approach to love, acting as a bridge to severe jealousy.

articles.title: Brain differences in dyslexia appear before children learn to read
articles.summary: Children who go on to develop dyslexia already show weaker brain responses to repeated written words in kindergarten, before formal reading lessons start. Their responses to faces, houses, and objects look much like those of their peers.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work
